evidence.quoted_text:
hint, not a proof of unique identity. The atomic `update-ref` zero-old-value
create still guards concurrent writers; after an occupied-ref race, recheck
the recorded identity before choosing another attempt number.
evidence.reason: The cited ADR relies on the atomic zero-old-value `update-ref` create as the concurrency guard, but that only serializes creation of the same exact ref. Two distinct identities that collide on the truncated candidate path can concurrently create different attempt refs (`a1` and `a2`); neither create races on an occupied ref, so neither rechecks and both identities can end up under the same candidate path. The ADR's conflict/extension rule is not atomic across attempt numbers, so this is a real gap in the described identity mechanism, not merely a request for optional hardening. Current contract evidence retains ADR-0007 as the task-ref identity rule, so it is not superseded.
